summary: Govind Vinayak Devasthali (1906–1994) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hari Damodar Velankar and served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).
Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indology scholar. He held posts at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda as a Professor (attested 1933–1939) and later as Director (attested 1953–1957).

Grace S. Fong is a Sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia (~1977–1984). She served as a Professor at Smith College (~1984–1990) and as Associate Professor and Department Chair at McGill University (~1992–2021).

Graeme MacQueen (1948–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1973–1979) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (~1973–1978) and served as a Lecturer at McMaster University (~1977–2003).

Grafton Elliot Smith (1871–1937) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School (~1888–1892), and St John's College (~1896–1899), later holding a post at University College London (~1919–1936).
Graham E. Clarke (d. 1998) worked in Tibetology and other fields. He held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and at the University of Oxford, where he was a Senior Member (attested 1998).
Graham Lock is a scholar in linguistics and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cambridge, St John's College, LSE under John Lane Bell, and Melbourne. He held posts at Melbourne (~2001), St Andrews (~2007), and CUNY Graduate Center (~2009).

Grant V. Aston is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004), studying under doctoral supervisor Jack Copeland and teacher Paul Harrison.

Graves Chamney Haughton (1788–1849) studied at Fort William College in Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor at East India Company College (1819–1827) and as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, which he founded.

Gray Tuttle is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history who earned his PhD at Harvard (2002). At Columbia University, he served as Associate Professor (attested 2008–2015) and Leila Hadley Luce Professor and Department Chair (attested 2026).

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was a linguist and Indologist. He founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873 and served as a Professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902.
Greg Bailey is an Indologist who studied under Madeleine Biardeau and doctoral supervisor J. Durham. He held academic posts at La Trobe University, attested in 1994 and as Professor in 2004.

Gregor Ahn studied at Copenhagen and Bonn under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit. Working in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he held posts at Münster (1992–1994), Tartu (1995), and served as Professor at Heidelberg University (1996–2025).

Gregory A. Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Virginia (1993), where he held a post (attested 2002), and became a Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. Educated at Columbia University, he has held posts at the University of Edinburgh and as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (both attested 2026).

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher (attested 2011) and Birgit Kellner, alongside multiple traditional teachers.

Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), completing doctoral supervision under Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University. He became Associate Professor at the University of California, Berkeley around 2000.

Gregory Price Grieve studied at San Francisco State and the University of Chicago. A religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.
